$comment: Written from crates/xenonet-model by cargo test -p xenonet-model. Change the type there, not this file.
title: An app
description: An app XenoNet knows sessions of, and what's fixed about it, as the app registry (core/apps.js) lists it. The apps XenoNet only observes have their id, name and numbat's names only.

id.description: What its session ids begin with: <id>:<the run's id>

numbat.description: The names numbat records its runs under

products.description: Its vendor products (<vendor>/<product>), each one of the provider drift check's, which lists their sources

env.description: The environment variable that moves its folder

default.description: Its folder when the variable isn't set

elsewhere.description: Files the variable moves too, which are elsewhere when it isn't set: each file's name, and the folder it's in then

context.description: Its context window, in tokens, until a transcript says otherwise

identity.description: The kind of account it runs under, as identity/v1 has it

limits.description: Its plan limits, as live/snapshot/v1's limits name them

team.description: The developer team that signs it, codesign's TeamIdentifier

format.description: Where and how XenoNet adds its hooks: Claude Code's settings.json, Codex's hooks.json, or Grok Build's hooks folder and config.toml

events.description: The hook events XenoNet adds, in order, each with the matcher it takes, if any

unheard.description: The hook events whose answers it passes over: XenoNet tells it nothing then, and keeps its messages for an event it hears

editTools.description: For a native reader, the tools whose calls are edits

has.description: What XenoNet can do with it at most; what it can do with a session is the session's own

counted.description: The map's stats count its sessions, under its id

headless.description: The arguments that run one turn with the prompt after them, for an agent an OpenShell sandbox runs

command.description: The program, by its name on the PATH; the app's adapter may find it elsewhere

acp.description: The command that runs it as an agent of the Agent Client Protocol, v1, for an app XenoNet starts sessions of over ACP

order.description: Where it goes among the candidates, from 1

description.description: What it's good for, as the decider reads it

routing.description: As a candidate for a routing suggestion: its place among the candidates and what it's good for

mcpStatus.description: Its own server lists the MCP servers it runs and their catalogs, which XenoNet asks when one of its sessions uses a server

names.description: The names it goes by, which no actor's name or product reads as

makers.description: Its makers, which no actor's product reads as

slugs.description: The actor slugs kept for it

reserved.description: What no actor may pass for: the names it goes by and its makers, and the actor slugs kept for it

reportsSpend.description: Its sessions report what they spent, which the spend view shows under its name

sorts.description: XenoNet runs turns of its own with it: the narration, and the sort of the projects folder into projects, whose picks name it as theirs

entries.description: The entries of one of its sessions' transcripts a handoff reads

clip.description: The characters of where the work left off that a brief for it keeps

handoff.description: How a handoff carries a session of it or to it, where that isn't 80 transcript entries read and 1500 characters kept of where the work left off
